newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Offshore oilfields eye Australia tropical low.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Offshore oilfields eye Australia tropical low.

text.p: The operator of the Barrow and Thevenard oil fields, West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET), said on Wednesday it was monitoring a tropical low threatening to build into a cyclone, but was maintaining production.
The low was located about 580 km off the Western Australia coastal town of Karratha at 0700 GMT (3.00 p.m.) and moving at about nine km an hour southeast, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
A low that far away is quite a distance, a spokesman for WAPET said ... "But that's not to say we're not monitoring developments."
The bureau said there was a chance the low would build into a category one cyclone -- the weakest in a scale of one-to-five -- in the next 24 hours
Barrow produces about 13,000 barrels per day of of crude while Thevenard's output is about 30,000 bpd

Earlier on Wednesday, the operator of the Cossack-Pioneer offshore oil rig, Woodside Petroleum Ltd, said it had evacuated non-essential personnel and taken other preliminary steps to disconnect from its mooring if the situation worsened.
WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh.

Equal-stake partners in the North West Shelf, where the Cossack Pioneer field is situated, are units of the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd -- a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp -- Chevron Corp, the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and operator Woodside Petroleum.
